title: Birbal and the Witch (മലയാളം)
summary: Hysteria grips Agra over rumors of a witch haunting the cemetery. Birbal investigates the supernatural terror and unmasks a band of thieves. [ML]
full_text:
Fear and hysteria gripped the citizens of Agra. For two weeks, terrifying rumors spread that a horrifying witch with backward feet, glowing red eyes, and wild hair was haunting the old cemetery on the outskirts of the city after midnight. Several night watchmen claimed to have heard bloodcurdling shrieks and seen dancing blue flames among the graves.

Citizens locked their doors at sunset, business in the night bazaars ground to a halt, and priests demanded heavy donations to perform expensive purification rituals.

Emperor Akbar was troubled by the panic. 'Birbal, the people are terrified. Some ministers urge me to deploy the army or hire exorcists from Bengal. What is your advice?'

Birbal replied calmly: 'Sire, darkness and superstition are close companions. Wherever people abandon reason, thieves and tricksters find their greatest profit. Give me one night, and I shall capture this "witch."'

At midnight, Birbal rode to the lonely cemetery accompanied only by four trusted guards armed with nets and lanterns. Hiding behind a marble tomb, they waited in absolute silence.

Soon after midnight, a terrifying wailing sound echoed through the mist. A bizarre, towering white figure with glowing blue sparks floating around its head drifted between the tombstones, uttering eerie incantations.

The guards began to tremble, but Birbal whispered: 'Look at the ground! The figure casts a solid shadow, and I smell burning sulfur and oil, not magic!'

Birbal signaled his men. They rushed from the shadows and threw a heavy hemp net over the screeching figure, pinning it to the earth!

Birbal struck his lantern. Beneath the white bedsheet stood no supernatural demon, but an infamous local bandit named Mangal, mounted upon wooden stilts! On his head was a hollow pumpkin carved with grinning teeth, filled with burning charcoal and sulfur to create the blue glow!

Further search of the mausoleum uncovered a hidden underground vault where Mangal's gang had been storing stolen gold, silver vessels, and silk looted from city merchants, using the 'witch' rumor to keep guards and citizens far away from their hideout!

The next morning, Birbal presented the unmasked bandit and his stilts before Emperor Akbar and the astonished court.

Birbal addressed the assembly: 'Fear is the real ghost, Your Majesty. When men allow fear to blind their intellect, a simple thief on wooden stilts becomes a demon of the underworld. Clear eyes and courage banish every phantom.'

Akbar commended Birbal's bravery and ordered the stolen wealth returned to the merchants, forever dispelling the ghost of Agra.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Birbal and the Witch"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
